items.hook: Muschelhaufen was a German annual, originally combining literature and graphic arts.
items.body: It was founded by Erik Martin from Viersen in 1969 and published – with an interruption of 11 years – until 2008, when the last issue came out. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: The Desperate Hours is a 1955 film noir starring Humphrey Bogart and Fredric March.
items.body: It was produced and directed by William Wyler and based on the 1954 novel and 1955 play of the same name, written by Joseph Hayes, which were loosely built on actual events. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Qui squadra mobile is an Italian television series starring Orazio Orlando and Luigi Vannucchi.
items.body: All 12 episodes were directed by Anton Giulio Majano and written by Massimo Felisatti, Anton Giulio Majano, and Fabio Pittorru. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The Sword and the Sickle is a novel by Mulk Raj Anand first published in 1942.
items.body: Like his other novels, this one also deals with the topic of social and political structures, specifically, the rise of Communism. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Wild chimpanzees teach youngsters by handing them tools
items.body: Adult chimpanzees have been observed passing tools to their younger relatives, helping them learn the skills needed for fishing for ants or algae
